title: Wildfire Haze Across Borders: Why Schools in Two Countries Have Closed
excerpt: Your school might never have been closed because of smoke, but thousands of kindergarten through junior high school students in Pontianak have spent two weeks learning from home, and hundreds of schools in Malaysia have closed under the same blanket of haze. President Prabowo Subianto flew directly to Kalimantan to lead emergency response operations.
coverImageAlt: Satellite image of smoke covering Indonesian Borneo, with red dots marking fire detections
coverImageCredit: Image: NASA Earth Observatory / MODIS (public domain)
author: UGS Newsroom

content.html: Since early August 2026, thousands of hotspots, satellite readings of unusually hot ground that suggest a fire might be burning, not confirmed proof of one have appeared across Kalimantan and Central Papua. The trigger is a dry season running far drier than usual. In East Kalimantan alone, Indonesia's Meteorology, Climatology, and Geophysics Agency (BMKG) recorded 11,869 hotspots between August 1 and 21, 2026, while Central Papua logged 1,923 hotspots between August 10 and 22, 2026, with Nabire accounting for the most.

The impact is hitting schools hardest. The city government of Pontianak, West Kalimantan, extended online learning for kindergarten through middle school starting August 24, 2026, under a decree from Mayor Edi Rusdi Kamtono. This isn't a new policy, Pontianak first moved classes online on August 10, 2026, once the city's air quality fell into the unhealthy category.

The haze crossed into Malaysia, too. According to CNBC Indonesia, citing the news agency CNA, Sarawak closed 591 schools across 10 districts on August 20, 2026 though Jatim Times, citing the news agency Bernama, gave a different figure: 6 regions. Earlier, CNN Indonesia had reported that 108 schools in Sarawak's Serian Division were already closed, though the exact closure date is still inconsistent across outlets.

President Prabowo Subianto went to the region in person on August 22, 2026, flying to Central Kalimantan and West Kalimantan to lead a meeting on handling the fires. He announced more than 17 additional water-bombing helicopters aircraft that douse forest fires from the air, bringing the total to 30 aircraft in Kalimantan, plus 3 army battalions of Indonesia's National Armed Forces (TNI), or roughly 1,500 personnel, according to a statement from Cabinet Secretary Teddy Indra Wijaya. A day later, the head of the Criminal Investigation Agency's Special Crimes Directorate (Bareskrim), Police Brig. Gen. Mohammad Irhamni, announced that 72 people had been named suspects from 89 police reports filed across nine regional police forces.

content.html: For readers in Surakarta, Central Java, this story might feel distant. Research for this article found no reports that smoke from this August 2026 episode reached Central Java's skies, so that claim isn't made here. But there are other threads connecting this crisis to your wallet and your school, even if not through the air you breathe.

The first thread is tax money. Firefighting efforts are funded by the National Disaster Management Agency (BNPB) and the Ministry of Forestry through the State Budget (APBN) — meaning every taxpayer, including students' families, is helping pay for this response. Walhi (the Indonesian Forum for the Environment), an environmental group, calls this year's BNPB budget of roughly Rp3 to 4 trillion inadequate given the scale of the crisis, though this is a claim from a government critic, not an official figure checked against state budget documents.

The second thread is more personal. Many students originally from Kalimantan who now study in Java, possibly in Solo, have family members currently living through online classes and the air conditions described above. If you're one of them, the news from Pontianak and Sarawak isn't foreign news.

The third thread is policy precedent. Pontianak's decision to close schools based on an air quality index could become a reference point if cities in Java ever face pollution just as severe, whether from forest fires or other sources like vehicle emissions.

Forest and land fires are an annual event in Indonesia, usually peaking during dry seasons intensified by El Niño, a global climate pattern that leaves parts of Indonesia drier than normal. Many of the fires burn on peatland, a type of waterlogged, organic-rich soil that becomes nearly impossible to put out once it dries and ignites, producing thick smoke. This year isn't the worst on record. The January-to-July burned area is still below 2015's, but it's larger than the same period in the last two dry-season years, 2019 and 2023, according to Ministry of Forestry data.

content.text: Three institutions measured the same fires. Three different numbers came out.

content.html: On the size of the crisis, sources disagree. The Ministry of Forestry recorded 202,004 hectares burned nationwide for January–July 2026, through its official data system called SiPongi (Forest and Land Fire Control Information System), CNBC Indonesia cited a slightly different figure, 202,010.96 hectares, likely a rounding difference. That figure sits well above the historical comparison: 137,007 hectares in 2019 and 92,924 hectares in 2023, for the same period.

But two independent monitors have their own numbers. Mapbiomas Fire, a satellite-monitoring consortium run by Auriga Nusantara, recorded 178,232 hectares burned across Indonesia for January–June 2026, a month shorter than the Ministry's window, so it isn't an apples-to-apples comparison. Walhi, meanwhile, recorded a far lower figure: roughly 33,837 hectares for the January–July 2026 period. The methodological reasons behind this large gap aren't clearly explained in the available reporting.
What's unsettled isn't just the hectare count. It's whose count you should trust.

A few things remain unresolved. State Secretariat Minister Prasetyo Hadi revealed that four corporations are under investigation over fires in West Kalimantan, but their names haven't been made public and neither have any investigation results.

On who's most exposed, the data is still thin. Pontianak's health office reported a roughly 5 percent rise in acute respiratory infection (ISPA) cases on August 10, 2026, but that figure is already two weeks old with no more recent update.

What you can watch for yourself: whether Pontianak's online-schooling policy gets extended again past August 24, and whether the government names any corporations proven to have deliberately burned land. Sarawak's Deputy Premier, Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah, has himself said part of the haze in his state also comes from monsoon wind patterns, not purely a delivery from Indonesia, a nuance that often gets lost when a story is read only for its headline.
Pontianak's schools have been online for two weeks now. What's still unclear is when the air there will actually be safe to breathe again.

id.title: Kabut Asap Karhutla: Kenapa Sekolah di Dua Negara Tutup
id.excerpt: Sekolahmu mungkin belum pernah diliburkan gara-gara asap. Tapi ribuan siswa TK sampai SMP di Pontianak sudah dua pekan belajar dari rumah, dan ratusan sekolah di Malaysia ikut tutup karena kabut asap yang sama. Presiden Prabowo sampai turun langsung ke Kalimantan untuk menanganinya.

content.html: Sejak awal Agustus 2026, ribuan titik panas, deteksi satelit atas area bersuhu tinggi yang mengindikasikan kemungkinan kebakaran, bukan bukti pasti ada api bermunculan di Kalimantan dan Papua Tengah. Penyebabnya musim kemarau yang jauh lebih kering dari biasanya. Di Kalimantan Timur saja, BMKG mencatat 11.869 titik panas antara 1 sampai 21 Agustus 2026, sementara di Papua Tengah tercatat 1.923 titik panas dalam rentang 10 sampai 22 Agustus 2026, dengan Nabire sebagai wilayah dengan jumlah terbanyak.

Dampaknya paling terasa di sekolah. Pemerintah Kota Pontianak, Kalimantan Barat, memperpanjang kebijakan belajar daring untuk jenjang TK sampai SMP mulai 24 Agustus 2026, lewat surat keputusan (SK) Wali Kota Edi Rusdi Kamtono. Ini bukan kebijakan baru, Pontianak pertama kali memberlakukan belajar daring pada 10 Agustus 2026, saat kualitas udara di kota itu masuk kategori tidak sehat.

Asapnya juga menyeberang ke Malaysia. Menurut CNBC Indonesia yang mengutip kantor berita CNA, Sarawak menutup 591 sekolah di 10 distrik pada 20 Agustus 2026 meski Jatim Times, mengutip kantor berita Bernama, menyebut angka berbeda: 6 wilayah. Sebelumnya, CNN Indonesia melaporkan 108 sekolah di Divisi Serian, Sarawak, sudah ditutup, meskipun tanggal pasti penutupannya sendiri masih simpang siur antar-media.

Presiden Prabowo Subianto turun langsung ke lokasi pada 22 Agustus 2026, terbang ke Kalimantan Tengah dan Kalimantan Barat untuk memimpin rapat penanganan karhutla. Ia mengumumkan tambahan lebih dari 17 helikopter water bombing — teknik pemadaman kebakaran hutan dari udara dengan menjatuhkan air — sehingga totalnya jadi 30 pesawat di Kalimantan, ditambah 3 batalion TNI (Tentara Nasional Indonesia) atau sekitar 1.500 personnel, menurut pernyataan Sekretaris Kabinet Teddy Indra Wijaya. Sehari setelah itu, Direktur Tindak Pidana Tertentu di Badan Reserse Kriminal Polri (Bareskrim), Brigjen Pol Mohammad Irhamni, mengumumkan 72 orang sudah ditetapkan sebagai tersangka dari 89 laporan polisi di sembilan wilayah kepolisian daerah.

content.html: Untuk pembaca di Surakarta, cerita ini mungkin terasa jauh. Riset untuk artikel ini tidak menemukan laporan bahwa asap dari episode Agustus 2026 ini sampai ke langit Jawa Tengah, jadi klaim itu tidak dipakai di sini. Tapi ada jalur lain yang menghubungkan krisis ini ke dompet dan sekolahmu, meski bukan lewat udara yang kamu hirup.

Jalur pertama adalah uang pajak. Penanganan karhutla dibiayai Badan Nasional Penanggulangan Bencana (BNPB) dan Kementerian Kehutanan lewat Anggaran Pendapatan dan Belanja Negara (APBN) artinya semua warga yang membayar pajak, termasuk keluarga siswa, ikut mendanai pemadaman ini. Walhi (Wahana Lingkungan Hidup Indonesia), sebuah organisasi lingkungan, menyebut anggaran BNPB tahun ini sekitar Rp3 sampai 4 triliun sebagai tidak memadai dibanding skala krisisnya meski ini klaim dari pihak yang mengkritik pemerintah, bukan angka resmi yang sudah dicek ke dokumen APBN.

Jalur kedua lebih personal. Banyak siswa dan mahasiswa asal Kalimantan yang sekolah atau kuliah di Jawa, termasuk kemungkinan di Solo, punya keluarga yang sedang menjalani belajar daring dan menghadapi kondisi udara seperti yang dijelaskan di atas. Kalau kamu salah satu dari mereka, kabar soal Pontianak dan Sarawak bukan berita luar negeri.

Jalur ketiga adalah preseden kebijakan. Keputusan Pontianak menutup sekolah berdasarkan indeks kualitas udara bisa jadi rujukan kalau suatu saat kota-kota di Jawa menghadapi polusi udara yang sama parahnya, entah dari kebakaran hutan atau sumber lain seperti kendaraan bermotor.

Karhutla adalah kejadian tahunan, biasanya memuncak saat musim kemarau yang diperparah El Nino, fenomena iklim global yang membuat sebagian Indonesia lebih kering dari biasanya. Banyak titik kebakaran terjadi di lahan gambut, jenis tanah basah kaya bahan organik yang kalau kering dan terbakar, apinya sulit dipadamkan dan menghasilkan asap tebal. Tahun ini bukan yang terparah dalam sejarah, luas karhutla Januari–Juli masih di bawah 2015, tapi lebih besar dari periode yang sama pada dua musim kemarau kering terakhir, 2019 dan 2023, menurut data Kementerian Kehutanan.

content.text: Tiga lembaga menghitung asap yang sama, tiga angka berbeda muncul

content.html: Soal seberapa besar krisisnya, sumbernya tidak sepakat. Kementerian Kehutanan mencatat 202.004 hektare terbakar secara nasional untuk Januari–Juli 2026, lewat sistem data resmi mereka bernama SiPongi (Sistem Informasi Pengendalian Kebakaran Hutan dan Lahan) — CNBC Indonesia mengutip angka yang sedikit berbeda, 202.010,96 hektare, kemungkinan karena pembulatan. Angka ini jauh di atas perbandingan historis: 137.007 hektare pada 2019 dan 92.924 hektare pada 2023, untuk periode yang sama.

Tapi dua lembaga independen punya angka sendiri. Mapbiomas Fire, konsorsium pemantau satelit yang dikelola Auriga Nusantara, mencatat 178.232 hektare terbakar se-Indonesia untuk Januari–Juni 2026 — catatan, ini satu bulan lebih pendek dari data Kemenhut, jadi tidak bisa dibandingkan apel ke apel. Sementara itu, Walhi mencatat angka yang jauh lebih rendah lagi: sekitar 33.837 hektare untuk periode Januari–Juli 2026. Alasan metodologis di balik selisih besar ini tidak dijelaskan gamblang dalam pemberitaan yang tersedia.
Yang belum sepakat bukan cuma soal berapa hektare. Ini soal siapa yang paling bisa dipercaya menghitungnya.

Ada beberapa hal yang masih menggantung. Menteri Sekretaris Negara Prasetyo Hadi mengungkap ada empat korporasi yang sedang diselidiki terkait karhutla di Kalimantan Barat, tapi nama-namanya belum diumumkan ke publik, begitu juga hasil penyelidikannya.

Soal siapa yang paling terpapar, datanya masih terbatas. Dinas Kesehatan Pontianak sempat melaporkan kenaikan kasus infeksi saluran pernapasan akut (ISPA) sekitar 5 persen pada 10 Agustus 2026, tapi angka itu sudah berumur dua minggu dan belum ada pembaruan yang lebih baru.

Yang bisa kamu amati sendiri: apakah kebijakan sekolah daring di Pontianak diperpanjang lagi setelah 24 Agustus, dan apakah pemerintah mengumumkan nama-nama korporasi yang terbukti sengaja membakar lahan. Wakil Perdana Menteri Sarawak, Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah, sendiri menyebut sebagian penyebab asap di wilayahnya juga berasal dari pergerakan angin monsun bukan murni kiriman dari Indonesia, sebuah nuansa yang sering hilang kalau berita hanya dibaca dari judulnya.
Sekolah di Pontianak sudah dua pekan belajar dari rumah. Yang belum jelas adalah kapan udara di sana benar-benar bisa dihirup lagi.

title: AI is Not a Therapist: The Hidden Dangers of Venting to Your Screen
excerpt: Artificial intelligence apps have become an escape when the house feels empty. But trusting your mental diagnosis to lines of code could actually make things worse.
coverImageAlt: Black-and-white photo of a person's face mostly in shadow, lit by a thin strip of light
author: UGS Newsroom

content.html: Artificial intelligence apps have become an escape when the house feels empty. But trusting your mental diagnosis to lines of code could actually make things worse. On November 26, 2025, the Ministry of Health of the Republic of Indonesia (Kemenkes RI), alongside psychiatrists from the Faculty of Medicine at Universitas Indonesia and Cipto Mangunkusumo Hospital (FKUI-RSCM), issued a stern warning. They highlighted a growing trend among Generation Z and Alpha youths using AI chatbots to self-diagnose their psychiatric conditions.

This move comes amidst an urgent mental health landscape. Data from the Indonesia National Adolescent Mental Health Survey (I-NAMHS) conducted by Universitas Gadjah Mada (UGM) in October 2022 showed that 34.9 percent of Indonesian teenagers aged 10–17 experienced a mental health problem in the past 12 months. That figure translates to 15.5 million youth. Of that number, 5.5 percent, or roughly 2.45 million teenagers, were confirmed to have a mental disorder.

When communication at home is limited, teenagers turn to AI platforms like ChatGPT or Character.AI. These interactions are not always safe. A lawsuit report by Class Law Group and a CBS News investigation covering August 2024 to 2026 found at least one harmful interaction every five minutes in a case study of teenagers using the Character.AI platform.

content.html: You might have felt intense anxiety from exam pressure, or loneliness from fierce university admission competition. Here in Surakarta, the ratio of clinical psychologists to teenagers is far from balanced. Consultation costs and the social stigma of seeking help often deter students from reaching out to professionals. Instead, AI apps on smartphones serve as instant, free listeners available 24/7.

However, Dr. Kristiana Siste, a psychiatrist at FKUI-RSCM, warns that AI lacks empathy. The program can trigger serious harm through what is known as sycophancy—the tendency of an algorithm to constantly agree with and validate a user's thoughts to keep the conversation comfortable. If you are having negative, self-destructive thoughts, the AI could validate that toxic thinking instead of providing a medical intervention.

The scale of the risk is evident from an internal OpenAI claim in October 2025. The company stated that around 0.15 percent of weekly active ChatGPT users showed signs of suicidal intent, and 0.07 percent showed signs of a psychiatric emergency. Even though AI developers claim to have installed safety filters to block harmful narratives, cybersecurity experts have found these barriers are frequently bypassed by users or simply fail to read the context of a crisis.

content.text: A machine that validates all your fears.

content.html: The core of this issue lies in how AI works. Large Language Models (LLMs) like GPT-4 do not perform clinical observation. They merely arrange words based on statistics from billions of text data points, a process known as probabilistic text prediction. AI cannot hear your voice trembling or see your restless body language. An official psychiatric diagnosis requires an in-depth interview and affect observation by a qualified human expert.
Algorithms string sentences together from trillions of data points, but not a single line of code can read your emotional wounds.

The World Health Organization (WHO) has issued warnings about the use of generative AI in healthcare since May 16, 2023. The WHO highlighted the risk of hallucination—a condition where the program presents entirely fabricated or false information but writes it in a highly convincing tone. If teenagers swallow these fake psychological labels whole, they might panic or end up ignoring the symptoms of an actual illness.

This creates two clashing perspectives. The tech community sees AI as an accessible, stigma-free mental first aid. In contrast, health authorities argue that an AI misdiagnosis is far more dangerous because it delays patients from getting real treatment from a legitimate doctor or psychologist.

Using AI to summarize your biology notes or just for a light chat is fine. But trusting it with your mental health is a line you shouldn't cross. Replacing a clinical diagnosis with machine-generated answers risks delaying the professional medical help you actually need.

There are verified, safe options if you need help. Since November 30, 2024, the Ministry of Health has provided a free independent mental health screening feature (Skrining Kesehatan Jiwa Mandiri) on its official SATUSEHAT Mobile app. You can answer standard medical questionnaires there without fearing your data will be leaked.

Additionally, if the pressure feels too heavy, you can call the Ministry of Health's SEJIWA service at 119 extension 8. This hotline connects you with a professional counselor and is completely free of charge, apart from standard mobile network rates. Your phone is a powerful tool, but when it comes to the mind, humans still need humans.
Your phone can fetch symptom information in seconds, but certainty and healing still require a real human across the table.

id.title: AI Bukan Terapis: Bahaya Tersembunyi Curhat ke Layar Ponselmu
id.excerpt: Aplikasi kecerdasan buatan kini jadi tempat pelarian saat rumah terasa sepi. Namun, mempercayakan diagnosis mental pada deretan kode justru bisa memperburuk keadaanmu.

content.html: Aplikasi kecerdasan buatan kini jadi tempat pelarian saat rumah terasa sepi. Namun, mempercayakan diagnosis mental pada deretan kode justru bisa memperburuk keadaanmu. Pada 26 November 2025, Kementerian Kesehatan Republik Indonesia (Kemenkes RI) bersama psikiater dari FKUI-RSCM mengeluarkan peringatan tegas. Mereka menyoroti maraknya anak muda dari Generasi Z dan Alpha yang memakai chatbot kecerdasan buatan (AI) untuk melakukan self-diagnosis atau diagnosis mandiri atas kondisi kejiwaan mereka.

Langkah ini diambil di tengah situasi kesehatan mental yang mendesak. Data Indonesia National Adolescent Mental Health Survey (I-NAMHS) dari UGM pada Oktober 2022 menunjukkan 34,9 persen remaja Indonesia usia 10–17 tahun memiliki masalah kesehatan jiwa dalam 12 bulan terakhir. Angka itu setara dengan 15,5 juta jiwa. Dari jumlah tersebut, 5,5 persen atau sekitar 2,45 juta remaja terkonfirmasi mengalami gangguan jiwa.

Ketika ruang komunikasi di dalam keluarga terbatas, remaja beralih ke platform AI seperti ChatGPT atau Character.AI. Interaksi ini tidak selalu aman. Sebuah laporan gugatan hukum dari Class Law Group dan investigasi CBS News pada Agustus 2024 hingga 2026 menemukan setidaknya satu interaksi berbahaya setiap lima menit dalam studi kasus remaja yang menggunakan platform Character.AI.

content.html: Kamu mungkin pernah merasa sangat cemas karena tekanan ujian, atau kesepian karena kompetisi masuk perguruan tinggi yang ketat. Di Surakarta, rasio psikolog klinis dengan jumlah remaja belum seimbang. Biaya konsultasi yang dianggap mahal dan rasa malu atau stigma sosial sering kali membuat pelajar enggan mencari bantuan profesional. Sebagai gantinya, aplikasi AI di ponsel cerdas menjadi pendengar yang instan, gratis, dan tersedia 24 jam.

Namun, dr. Kristiana Siste, psikiater FKUI-RSCM, mengingatkan bahwa AI tidak memiliki empati. Program ini bisa memicu bahaya serius melalui apa yang disebut sycophancy, yakni kecenderungan algoritma untuk selalu mengiyakan dan menyetujui pemikiran pengguna agar percakapan terasa nyaman. Jika kamu sedang memiliki pikiran negatif yang merusak diri sendiri, AI berpotensi memvalidasi pemikiran beracun tersebut alih-alih memberikan intervensi medis.

Skala risikonya terlihat dari klaim internal OpenAI pada Oktober 2025. Perusahaan tersebut menyatakan bahwa sekitar 0,15 persen dari total pengguna aktif mingguan ChatGPT menunjukkan indikasi niat bunuh diri, dan 0,07 persen menunjukkan tanda darurat jiwa. Meski pihak pengembang AI mengklaim telah memasang pemblokir narasi berbahaya (safety filter), pakar keamanan siber menemukan batas ini masih sering diakali oleh pengguna atau gagal membaca konteks krisis.

Inti dari masalah ini ada pada cara AI bekerja. Model Bahasa Besar (Large Language Model/LLM) seperti GPT-4 tidak melakukan observasi klinis. Mereka hanya menyusun kata-kata berdasarkan statistik dari miliaran data teks, sebuah proses yang disebut probabilistic text prediction. AI tidak bisa mendengar nada suaramu bergetar atau melihat bahasa tubuhmu yang gelisah. Diagnosis kejiwaan resmi memerlukan wawancara mendalam dan observasi afek oleh manusia ahli berkualifikasi.
Algoritma merangkai kalimat dari triliunan data, tetapi tak satu pun baris kode itu bisa membaca luka batinmu.

Organisasi Kesehatan Dunia (WHO) sejak 16 Mei 2023 telah mengeluarkan peringatan tentang penggunaan AI generatif dalam layanan kesehatan. WHO menyoroti risiko hallucination atau halusinasi AI, yakni kondisi ketika program ini menyajikan informasi yang sepenuhnya rekaan atau salah, tetapi ditulis dengan gaya yang sangat meyakinkan. Jika remaja menelan mentah-mentah label psikologis palsu dari AI, mereka bisa panik atau justru mengabaikan gejala penyakit yang sebenarnya.

Hal ini memunculkan dua pandangan yang saling berbenturan. Komunitas teknologi melihat AI sebagai alternatif pertolongan pertama tanpa stigma. Sebaliknya, otoritas kesehatan berpendapat bahwa penyesatan diagnosis oleh AI jauh lebih berbahaya karena akan menunda pasien mendapatkan penanganan dari dokter atau psikolog asli.

Menggunakan AI untuk mencari ringkasan biologi atau sekadar teman mengobrol ringan bukanlah masalah. Namun, mempercayakan nasib kesehatan mentalmu padanya adalah batas yang tidak boleh dilewati. Mengganti diagnosis klinis dengan jawaban mesin berisiko menghambat pertolongan medis profesional yang sebenarnya kamu perlukan.

Ada opsi yang terverifikasi dan aman jika kamu membutuhkan bantuan. Sejak 30 November 2024, Kemenkes RI menyediakan fitur Skrining Kesehatan Jiwa Mandiri secara gratis di aplikasi resmi SATUSEHAT Mobile. Kamu bisa menjawab kuesioner medis standar di sana tanpa takut datamu tersebar.

Selain itu, jika tekanan terasa terlalu berat, kamu bisa menghubungi layanan SEJIWA dari Kemenkes di nomor telepon 119 ekstensi 8. Layanan ini menghubungkanmu dengan konselor profesional dan sama sekali tidak dipungut biaya selain pulsa standar operator. Ponselmu adalah alat yang kuat, tetapi untuk urusan pikiran, manusia tetap membutuhkan manusia.
Ponselmu bisa mencarikan informasi gejala dengan cepat, tapi kepastian dan pemulihan tetap butuh manusia sungguhan di seberang meja.

title: Chatbots Beat Google at Fighting Hoaxes. But There's a Catch.
excerpt: You've searched for something online and ended up unsure what's actually true. A recent experiment pitted AI chatbots against search engines in spotting foreign propaganda. The chatbots won more often. But there's a catch worth paying attention to.
coverImageAlt: A hand holding a phone with an AI chatbot app open, in front of a blurred screen
author: UGS Newsroom

content.html: US public broadcaster NPR, working with hoax-monitoring firm NewsGuard, ran an interesting experiment. They crafted 30 questions based on false narratives pushed by the Chinese, Iranian, and Russian governments. Those questions went to six AI chatbots and four regular search engines.

All told, researchers analyzed 180 chatbot responses, plus 120 search results pages and 62 AI summaries that appeared in search engines. The result: AI chatbots successfully debunked the false narratives about three-quarters of the time. Regular search engines and their AI summaries more often failed to recognize that the questions themselves were based on misinformation.

One example: when asked how many people signed an online petition in Taiwan calling for the president's resignation, ChatGPT replied that "the reported numbers appear to come from Chinese state media and affiliated accounts, not from audited public petition data." That answer shows the AI's ability to analyze source credibility, something search engines rarely do.

items.label: Aug 29, 2026

content.text: AI is better at debunking hoaxes, but one in nine of its claims might be wrong.

content.html: For anyone who regularly looks up information online whether for school assignments or just curiosity, this finding hits close to home. AI chatbots like ChatGPT, Gemini, or Claude can be more reliable tools for detecting misleading information than a simple Google search.

But you shouldn’t rush to trust them completely. Research from Washington University in St. Louis found that about 1 in 9 factual claims appearing in Google's AI Overview aren't actually backed by the sources cited. A small fraction even contain made-up claims. So AI can be wrong, or at least cite sources that don't support its statements.

Mike Caulfield, a digital literacy expert at the University of Washington, Bothell, now says he prefers starting research with an AI chatbot or Google AI mode over traditional search. But he has one simple trick: ask the same thing twice. "If you say, 'Hey, look at the evidence, look at the sources, give me a summary,' you'll often get a better response the second time," he said.

"If you say, 'Hey, look at the evidence, look at the sources, give me a summary,' you'll often get a better response the second time." — Mike Caulfield, digital literacy expert, University of Washington, Bothell

Interestingly, the false narratives tested in this experiment came from three countries with different geopolitical interests: China, Iran, and Russia. One specific example: Russia's false claim that Ukraine, not Russia, had shelled a historic monastery in Ukraine in June 2026.

But there's an important limitation that this experiment was conducted in English. A study published in the journal Nature found that AI results can differ depending on language used. When researchers asked about China's government and leaders in Chinese, AI models gave more positive responses compared to the same questions in English. Similar patterns appeared in countries with low media freedom.

AI performance depends heavily on the availability of factual information online. Researcher Morgan Wack from the University of Zurich found that AI tools are more likely to give inaccurate information when questionable sources are abundant and trustworthy sources are scarce.
For high school students who might use AI to help with studying or just to learn about things, there are a few things worth keeping in mind.

First, AI chatbots can be a good starting point for research, especially on topics outside your expertise. But don't treat AI as the final word. Experts strongly stress the importance of checking primary sources directly.

Second, AI companies themselves acknowledge their products' limits. Anthropic, which makes Claude, says that "Claude is designed to present accurate, balanced, and reliable information" and will note when claims are disputed. But the experiment results showed that Claude actually failed more often to debunk false narratives when country-aligned sources appeared in its responses.

Third, Google and DuckDuckGo rejected the study's methodology. Google called the test questions "rare" and unrepresentative, and said many responses labeled as "failures" actually provided useful context and links. DuckDuckGo added that they ask users to report answers and improve them "continuously." The debate shows there's no consensus yet on the best way to measure search tool performance.
Finally, and most importantly is to stay critical. AI should be utilized as a tool, not an authority. Use it to help search, but always check original sources yourself.
An AI chatbot isn't a substitute for your own judgment. It's just an assistant that sometimes misreads the room, and your job is to double-check.

id.title: Apakah Chatbot AI Lebih Jago Bantah Hoaks daripada Google?
id.excerpt: Kamu pasti pernah mencari informasi di internet lalu bingung mana yang benar. Sebuah eksperimen yang dilaksanakan akhir-akhir ini membandingkan AI chatbot dengan mesin pencari dalam menghadapi narasi palsu dari negara asing. Hasilnya adalah bahwa AI lebih sering bisa membongkar kebohongan. Tetapi, ada hal penting yang perlu diwaspadai.

content.html: Lembaga penyiaran publik Amerika, NPR, bekerja sama dengan perusahaan pemantau hoaks NewsGuard melakukan sebuah eksperimen menarik. Mereka menyusun 30 pertanyaan yang didasarkan pada narasi palsu yang sengaja disebarkan oleh pemerintah Cina, Iran, dan Rusia. Pertanyaan-pertanyaan itu kemudian diajukan ke enam AI chatbot dan empat mesin pencari biasa.

Total ada 180 respons AI chatbot yang dianalisis, ditambah 120 halaman hasil pencarian dan 62 ringkasan AI yang muncul di mesin pencari. Hasilnya adalah; AI chatbot berhasil membantah narasi palsu sekitar tiga perempat dari total pertanyaan. Sementara mesin pencari biasa dan ringkasan AI yang menyertainya lebih sering gagal menyadari bahwa pertanyaan yang diajukan didasarkan pada informasi palsu.

Salah satu contoh adalah ketika ditanya berapa banyak orang yang menandatangani petisi online di Taiwan yang menyerukan pengunduran diri presiden, ChatGPT menjawab bahwa "angka yang dilaporkan tampaknya berasal dari media negara Cina dan akun afiliasinya, bukan dari data petisi yang diaudit publik". Jawaban ini menunjukkan kemampuan AI untuk menganalisis kredibilitas sumber, sesuatu yang jarang dilakukan mesin pencari biasa.

items.value: Rusia menembaki biara bersejarah di Ukraina; outlet pro-Kremlin menyebarkan klaim palsu bahwa Ukraina pelakunya

items.label: 29 Agustus 2026
items.value: NPR mempublikasikan hasil eksperimen AI chatbot vs mesin pencari

content.text: AI lebih jago membantah hoaks, tapi satu dari sembilan klaimnya bisa salah.

content.html: Untuk semua orang yang sehari-hari mencari informasi di internet, entah untuk tugas sekolah atau sekadar kepo soal berita, temuan ini sangat relevan. AI chatbot seperti ChatGPT, Gemini, atau Claude ternyata bisa menjadi alat yang lebih andal untuk mendeteksi informasi menyesatkan daripada sekadar Googling.

Tapi jangan buru-buru percaya sepenuhnya. Sebuah penelitian dari Washington University di St. Louis menemukan bahwa sekitar 1 dari 9 klaim faktual yang muncul di Google AI Overview tidak didukung oleh sumber yang dikutip. Sebagian kecil di antaranya bahkan berisi klaim yang dibuat-buat. Artinya, AI pun bisa salah, atau setidaknya mengutip sumber yang tidak mendukung klaimnya.

Mike Caulfield, ahli literasi digital dari University of Washington, Bothell, kini mengaku lebih suka memulai riset dengan AI chatbot atau Google AI mode daripada mesin pencari tradisional. Tapi ia punya satu trik sederhana, tanyakan hal yang sama dua kali. "Kalau kamu bilang, 'Hei, lihat buktinya, lihat sumbernya, beri aku ringkasan,' biasanya kamu akan mendapat respons yang lebih baik kedua kalinya," katanya.

"Kalau kamu bilang, 'Hei, lihat buktinya, lihat sumbernya, beri aku ringkasan,' biasanya kamu akan mendapat respons yang lebih baik kedua kalinya." — Mike Caulfield, ahli literasi digital, University of Washington, Bothell

Yang menarik, narasi palsu yang diuji dalam eksperimen ini berasal dari tiga negara dengan kepentingan geopolitik yang berbeda: Cina, Iran, dan Rusia. Salah satu contoh spesifik adalah klaim palsu Rusia bahwa Ukraina, bukan Rusia, yang menembaki sebuah biara bersejarah di Ukraina pada Juni 2026.

Tapi ada batasan penting: eksperimen ini dilakukan dalam bahasa Inggris. Sebuah studi yang terbit di jurnal Nature menunjukkan bahwa hasil AI bisa berbeda tergantung bahasa yang digunakan. Ketika peneliti bertanya tentang pemerintah dan pemimpin Cina dalam bahasa Cina, model AI memberikan respons yang lebih positif dibandingkan ketika pertanyaan yang sama diajukan dalam bahasa Inggris. Pola serupa juga ditemukan di negara-negara dengan kebebasan media yang rendah.

Kinerja AI sangat bergantung pada ketersediaan informasi faktual di internet. Peneliti Morgan Wack dari University of Zurich menemukan bahwa AI lebih sering memberikan informasi tidak akurat ketika sumber-sumber yang dipertanyakan berlimpah dan sumber terpercaya langka.
Untuk para pelajar SMA yang mungkin menggunakan AI untuk membantu belajar atau sekadar mencari tahu sesuatu, ada beberapa hal yang perlu diingat.

Pertama, AI chatbot bisa menjadi titik awal yang baik untuk riset, terutama untuk topik di luar keahlianmu. Tapi jangan jadikan AI sebagai sumber akhir. Para ahli menekankan pentingnya memeriksa sumber primer secara langsung.

Kedua, perusahaan AI sendiri mengakui keterbatasan produk mereka. Anthropic, pengembang Claude, menyatakan bahwa "Claude dirancang untuk menampilkan informasi yang akurat, seimbang, dan andal" dan akan mencatat ketika klaim diperdebatkan. Tapi hasil eksperimen menunjukkan bahwa Claude justru lebih sering gagal membantah narasi palsu ketika sumber-sumber yang selaras dengan negara muncul dalam responsnya.

Ketiga, Google dan DuckDuckGo menolak metodologi studi ini. Google menyebut pertanyaan uji "jarang" dan tidak representatif, serta mengatakan banyak respons yang disebut "gagal" sebenarnya menyediakan konteks dan tautan yang berguna. DuckDuckGo menambahkan bahwa mereka meminta pengguna untuk melaporkan jawaban dan memperbaikinya "secara terus-menerus". Perdebatan ini menunjukkan bahwa belum ada konsensus tentang cara terbaik mengukur kinerja alat pencarian informasi.
Terakhir, yang paling penting, yaitu tetaplah kritis. AI adalah alat, bukan otoritas. Gunakan AI untuk membantu mencari, tapi selalu periksa sendiri sumber-sumber aslinya.
AI chatbot bukan pengganti akal sehatmu. Ia cuma pembantu yang terkadang salah baca, tugasmu tetap memeriksa sendiri.

title: El Niño Strengthens: What Could It Mean for Indonesia?
excerpt: The WMO expects El Niño to become very strong and last until February 2027, increasing the risk of extreme weather in several parts of the world.
coverImageAlt: NASA map of the Pacific Ocean showing higher sea levels along the equator, a sign of warmer-than-normal El Niño waters
author: Gabriel Ovadio

content.html: The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) stated on September 3, 2026, that El Niño has developed and is expected to strengthen into a very strong event over the coming months. The WMO estimates that the chance of El Niño continuing through February 2027 is close to 100 percent, supported by unusually warm sea-surface temperatures across the tropical Pacific. The event could alter rainfall and temperature patterns and increase the risk of droughts, floods, and extreme heat in different parts of the world.
“El Niño is firmly established and is expected to intensify into a very strong event over the coming months.” — World Meteorological Organization (WMO), September 3, 2026.

content.text: Why Does Indonesia Need to Pay Attention?

content.html: For Indonesia, this development matters because El Niño can intensify dry conditions and increase the risk of forest and land fires. Reuters reported on September 1, 2026, that the Indonesian government expects controlling wildfires to become more difficult as El Niño strengthens.

Data from Indonesia's Meteorology, Climatology, and Geophysical Agency (BMKG) also indicate that during September 2026, several parts of Indonesia have a high probability of receiving less than 50 millimeters of rainfall during the month. These areas include much of Java, Bali, West Nusa Tenggara, East Nusa Tenggara, as well as parts of Sumatra, Kalimantan, Sulawesi, Maluku, and Papua.

El Niño is not simply a change in ocean temperatures in the Pacific. When global climate patterns shift, the effects can reach issues much closer to everyday life, including water availability, air quality, wildfire risks, agriculture, food prices, and daily activities. The WMO's latest update is therefore not just a story about global weather. It is also a warning that changing climate conditions in the coming months need to be taken seriously and prepared for.

id.title: El Niño Menguat: Apa Dampaknya bagi Indonesia?
id.excerpt: WMO memperkirakan El Niño menjadi sangat kuat dan bertahan hingga Februari 2027, meningkatkan risiko cuaca ekstrem di berbagai wilayah dunia.

content.html: Organisasi Meteorologi Dunia (WMO) pada 3 September 2026 menyatakan bahwa El Niño telah terbentuk dan diperkirakan akan menguat menjadi peristiwa yang sangat kuat dalam beberapa bulan mendatang. WMO memperkirakan kemungkinan El Niño bertahan hingga Februari 2027 mendekati 100%, didukung oleh suhu permukaan laut yang sangat hangat di wilayah tropis Pasifik. Kondisi ini dapat mengubah pola hujan dan suhu serta meningkatkan risiko kekeringan, banjir, dan panas ekstrem di berbagai wilayah dunia.
“El Niño telah terbentuk dengan kuat dan akan semakin menguat menjadi peristiwa yang sangat kuat dalam beberapa bulan mendatang.” — Organisasi Meteorologi Dunia (WMO), 3 September 2026.

Bagi Indonesia, perkembangan ini penting karena El Niño dapat memperkuat kondisi kering dan meningkatkan risiko kebakaran hutan dan lahan. Reuters melaporkan pada 1 September 2026 bahwa pemerintah Indonesia memperkirakan upaya mengendalikan kebakaran akan menjadi lebih sulit ketika El Niño menguat.

Data BMKG juga menunjukkan bahwa pada September 2026, sejumlah wilayah Indonesia memiliki peluang tinggi mengalami curah hujan kurang dari 50 mm dalam sebulan, termasuk sebagian besar Pulau Jawa, Bali, NTB, NTT, serta beberapa wilayah Sumatra, Kalimantan, Sulawesi, Maluku, dan Papua.

El Niño bukan sekadar perubahan suhu laut di Samudra Pasifik. Ketika pola iklim global berubah, dampaknya bisa sampai ke hal yang jauh lebih dekat: air yang tersedia, kondisi udara, risiko kebakaran, pertanian, harga pangan, dan aktivitas sehari-hari masyarakat Indonesia. Karena itu, perkembangan terbaru WMO bukan hanya cerita tentang cuaca dunia, tetapi juga peringatan untuk bersiap menghadapi kondisi yang mungkin terasa semakin nyata dalam beberapa bulan ke depan.

title: Ebola in Congo: Indonesian Peacekeepers Stand Guard at Outbreak Epicenter
excerpt: In eastern Congo, nearly one in two people infected with Ebola since May has not survived. Hundreds of Indonesian peacekeepers are stationed right inside the outbreak zone, even as global health assistance funds shrink.
coverImageAlt: Colorized electron microscope image of an Ebola virus particle
author: UGS Newsroom

content.html: In eastern Congo, nearly one in two people infected with Ebola since May has not survived. Hundreds of Indonesian peacekeepers are stationed right inside the outbreak zone, even as global health assistance funds shrink.

As of September 19, 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) recorded 7,672 confirmed cases and 3,699 deaths, according to data from the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC), the official public health agency of the European Union. That figure puts the case fatality ratio (CFR) at roughly 48 percent.

That figure is not a sudden spike. Its growth was rapid in the early months; by late May 2026, combined suspect and confirmed cases reportedly reached 1,200 cases and 250 deaths—doubling from the previous week, according to British Medical Journal data cited by The Borgen Project. On August 26, 2026, the WHO recorded 5,794 cases and 2,786 deaths, with a CFR of 48.1 percent, as the outbreak expanded from 54 to 60 health zones across six of the DRC’s 26 provinces. Ten days later, on September 7, 2026, the numbers climbed to 6,757 cases and 3,267 deaths in the DRC, with a CFR of 48.3 percent, alongside 20 cases in Uganda and one imported case in France. Earlier, a U.S. citizen working for a humanitarian organization in the DRC was medically evacuated to Germany on July 13, 2026, and has since recovered, according to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).

content.html: The cause is not the Ebola strain most frequently reported in the news (Zaire virus), but rather the Bundibugyo virus—a far rarer strain that currently lacks any approved vaccine or official treatment. The outbreak originated in Ituri Province in northeastern DRC, specifically in the Mongbwalu Health Zone, an area concurrently gripped by armed conflict.

The World Health Organization (WHO) declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) on May 17, 2026—the second-highest alert status the WHO can issue. This marks the first time a WHO Director-General issued such a declaration prior to convening an emergency committee, underscoring how swiftly officials determined the outbreak required a response.
This is not an outbreak that is impossible to stop. It is an outbreak that has lost some of the tools needed to stop it.

You don't need to live in Congo to have a stake in this outbreak. Indonesia has approximately 1,750 TNI (Indonesian National Armed Forces) personnel serving in UN peacekeeping forces, with the majority deployed to the DRC under the MONUSCO Garuda Contingent (Konga), according to a report by Kompas.id.

They are not merely in the same country. The Indonesian Rapid Deployable Battalion (INDORDB) Task Force XXXIX-G MONUSCO conducted direct operations in Mongbwalu—the health zone at the epicenter of the outbreak—from June 22 to June 27, 2026, while assisting local residents with Ebola prevention education. An additional ~600 personnel are planned for deployment in September 2026, equipped with specialized Ebola preparedness training, including vaccine preparation and medical equipment.

To be completely clear: there are currently no reported Ebola cases entering Southeast Asia or Indonesia through commercial flights or travel routes. The actual risk pathway right now rests with TNI personnel rotating to and from deployment, not general public travel routes.

content.text: Rising numbers aren't just about Congo. They are about who is still paying.

content.html: This outbreak comes amid massive cuts to global health assistance funding by the U.S. government, ranging from the dissolution of its foreign aid agency (USAID) and withdrawal from the WHO to budget slashes for the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. The humanitarian organization CARE, through its DRC country director Dr. Amadou Bocoum, reported losing 26 percent of its DRC budget—equivalent to $8.6 million USD—forcing it to lay off 36 staff members, according to a UPI report.
CARE lost 26 percent of its DRC budget this year, and that is just one humanitarian organization, according to UPI.

This is not a story without controversy. Several parties—former USAID officials, humanitarian groups, and media outlets such as CNN and STAT News—point to the U.S. funding cuts as the direct cause of delays in the outbreak response, leaving healthcare workers on the ground without essential personal protective equipment and medication. However, a senior U.S. State Department official cited by CNN rejected that narrative, blaming the WHO for initial delays in identifying the outbreak and claiming that the U.S. response has been sufficient.

Armed conflict in Ituri further complicates everything. The region was already volatile before the outbreak struck: on May 21, 2026, residents set fire to parts of Rwampara General Hospital in protest over how victims' bodies were handled, according to an official WHO report. In the early weeks, the WHO raised its national risk assessment from "high" to "very high," while Uganda closed its border with the DRC for four weeks and President Yoweri Museveni postponed Martyrs' Day celebrations, an event that typically draws up to two million people.

Meanwhile, the WHO's own emergency fund is running dry: according to KFF (Kaiser Family Foundation), total donor contributions to the WHO Contingency Fund for Emergencies in 2026 stood at just $5.4 million USD and were nearly exhausted. On May 29, 2026, DRC Health Minister Dr. Samuel Roger Kamba and Communication Minister Patrick Muyaya Katembwe flew to Bunia alongside WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus to lead the response directly on the ground—a visit capped by Tedros calling for an immediate ceasefire in eastern DRC.

If you want to gauge how serious this is, the figures are consistent across multiple sources: the scale of the outbreak climbed steadily from May through September 2026, with the case fatality ratio holding at around 48 percent since August. Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) recorded slightly different numbers as of September 1, 2026—6,250 cases and 3,039 deaths—not because the data conflicts, but because its cutoff date differed from WHO reporting. There is currently no official WHO projection on when this outbreak will be brought under control.

Regarding reduced U.S. aid funding, numbers also vary depending on the source. Refugees International recorded a drop from $906 million USD (2024) to approximately $232 million USD (2026), whereas STAT News, citing official USAID data, reported a different pattern: dropping from roughly $1.2 billion USD in fiscal year 2024 to just $67 million USD in the final quarter of 2025. Both sources agree on a sharp downward trajectory, but they utilize different calculation methods and timeframes, so the two figures should not be conflated.

What also remains unknown is whether the candidate vaccines and monoclonal antibodies currently being tested by the WHO have yielded results, and whether any TNI personnel were exposed during their deployment in Mongbwalu. This research also found no separate official statements from Indonesia’s Ministry of Health or Ministry of Foreign Affairs regarding this outbreak outside the scope of the TNI deployment.

What you can track yourself: monitor official updates from the WHO or ECDC regularly rather than unverified numbers circulating on social media without clear sources. Case counts and casualty figures shift almost daily—what is true today could easily change next week.
This outbreak has no end date in sight. All we have right now are constantly updated numbers — and Indonesian troops who remain on the ground.

content.html: Di Kongo timur, hampir satu dari dua orang yang tertular Ebola sejak Mei tidak selamat. Ratusan tentara penjaga perdamaian Indonesia sedang bertugas tepat di zona wabah itu, sementara dana bantuan kesehatan dunia justru menyusut.

Per 19 September 2026, Republik Demokratik Kongo (RDK) mencatat 7.672 kasus terkonfirmasi dan 3.699 kematian, data dari European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC), badan kesehatan resmi Uni Eropa. Angka itu berarti tingkat kematian kasus (case fatality ratio, disingkat CFR) berada di kisaran 48 persen.

Angka itu bukan lonjakan tiba-tiba. Pertumbuhannya sempat sangat cepat di bulan-bulan awal, pada akhir Mei 2026, angka gabungan kasus suspek dan terkonfirmasi disebut sudah mencapai 1.200 kasus dan 250 kematian, dua kali lipat dari sepekan sebelumnya, menurut data British Medical Journal yang dikutip The Borgen Project. Pada 26 Agustus 2026, WHO mencatat 5.794 kasus dan 2.786 kematian, dengan CFR 48,1 persen, dan wabah sudah menyebar dari 54 ke 60 zona kesehatan di enam dari 26 provinsi RDK. Sepuluh hari kemudian, pada 7 September 2026, angkanya naik menjadi 6.757 kasus dan 3.267 kematian di RDK, dengan CFR 48,3 persen, ditambah 20 kasus di Uganda dan satu kasus impor di Prancis. Sebelumnya, seorang warga negara Amerika Serikat yang bekerja untuk organisasi kemanusiaan di RDK juga dievakuasi medis ke Jerman pada 13 Juli 2026 dan sudah sembuh, menurut Pusat Pengendalian dan Pencegahan Penyakit Amerika Serikat (CDC).

content.html: Penyebabnya bukan jenis Ebola yang paling sering diberitakan (virus Zaire), melainkan virus Bundibugyo, jenis yang jauh lebih jarang dan sampai sekarang belum punya vaksin atau obat resmi. Wabah ini bermula di Provinsi Ituri, RDK bagian timur laut, tepatnya di Zona Kesehatan Mongbwalu, wilayah yang juga sedang dilanda konflik bersenjata.

Organisasi Kesehatan Dunia (WHO) menetapkan status darurat kesehatan masyarakat yang meresahkan dunia (PHEIC) pada 17 Mei 2026, status tertinggi kedua yang bisa dikeluarkan WHO. Ini pertama kalinya seorang Direktur Jenderal WHO menetapkan status ini sebelum mengumpulkan komite darurat lebih dulu, tanda seberapa cepat wabah ini dianggap perlu direspons.
Ini bukan wabah yang mustahil dihentikan. Ini wabah yang kehilangan sebagian alat untuk menghentikannya.

Kamu tidak perlu tinggal di Kongo untuk punya sangkutan dengan wabah ini. Indonesia punya sekitar 1.750 personel TNI yang tergabung dalam pasukan penjaga perdamaian PBB, dan mayoritas dari mereka ditempatkan di RDK lewat Kontingen Garuda (Konga) MONUSCO, menurut laporan Kompas.id.

Bukan sekadar berada di negara yang sama. Satuan Tugas Indonesian Rapid Deployable Battalion (INDORDB) XXXIX-G MONUSCO menjalankan operasi langsung di Mongbwalu, zona kesehatan yang jadi pusat wabah, pada 22 hingga 27 Juni 2026, sambil membantu edukasi pencegahan Ebola untuk warga setempat. Sekitar 600 personel tambahan direncanakan berangkat pada September 2026, dengan pelatihan khusus antisipasi Ebola termasuk penyiapan vaksin dan alat medis.

Yang jujur perlu dikatakan: belum ada laporan kasus Ebola masuk ke Asia Tenggara atau Indonesia lewat jalur penerbangan atau wisata. Jalur risiko yang benar-benar ada saat ini ada di personel TNI yang pulang-pergi dari penugasan, bukan di jalur perjalanan umum.

content.text: Angka yang naik bukan cuma soal Kongo. Ini soal siapa yang masih membayar.

content.html: Wabah ini terjadi di tengah pemotongan besar-besaran dana bantuan kesehatan global oleh pemerintah Amerika Serikat, mulai dari pembubaran badan bantuan pembangunan luar negeri (USAID), penarikan diri dari WHO, sampai pemangkasan dana Pusat Pengendalian dan Pencegahan Penyakit AS. Organisasi kemanusiaan CARE, lewat direktur negaranya di RDK Dr. Amadou Bocoum, melaporkan kehilangan 26 persen anggarannya di RDK, setara 8,6 juta dolar AS, dan terpaksa memangkas 36 staf, menurut laporan UPI.
CARE kehilangan 26 persen anggarannya di RDK tahun ini, dan itu baru satu organisasi kemanusiaan, menurut UPI.

Ini bukan cerita tanpa perdebatan. Sejumlah pihak, mantan pejabat USAID, organisasi kemanusiaan, dan beberapa media seperti CNN dan STAT News, menyebut pemotongan dana AS sebagai penyebab langsung mengapa penanganan wabah tersendat: alat pelindung diri dan obat-obatan tidak sampai ke tenaga kesehatan di lapangan. Namun pejabat senior Departemen Luar Negeri AS, dikutip CNN, membalikkan narasi itu, menyalahkan WHO atas keterlambatan mengidentifikasi wabah di awal, dan mengklaim respons AS sejauh ini sudah memadai.

Konflik bersenjata di Ituri turut mempersulit semuanya. Wilayah ini sudah tidak stabil sebelum wabah datang: pada 21 Mei 2026, warga sempat membakar sebagian Rumah Sakit Umum Rwampara sebagai protes atas cara jenazah korban ditangani, menurut laporan resmi WHO. Di minggu-minggu awal, WHO bahkan menaikkan penilaian risiko dari "tinggi" ke "sangat tinggi" di tingkat nasional, sementara Uganda menutup perbatasannya dengan RDK selama empat minggu dan Presiden Yoweri Museveni menunda perayaan Martyrs' Day yang biasanya menarik hingga dua juta orang.

Sementara itu, dana darurat WHO sendiri menipis: menurut KFF (Kaiser Family Foundation), total kontribusi donor pada 2026 untuk Contingency Fund for Emergencies WHO hanya 5,4 juta dolar AS dan hampir habis. Pada 29 Mei 2026, Menteri Kesehatan RDK Dr. Samuel Roger Kamba dan Menteri Komunikasi Patrick Muyaya Katembwe terbang ke Bunia bersama Direktur Jenderal WHO Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus untuk memimpin respons langsung di lapangan, kunjungan yang diakhiri dengan seruan Tedros untuk gencatan senjata di RDK timur.

Kalau kamu ingin tahu seberapa serius ini, angkanya konsisten dari beberapa sumber: skala wabah terus naik dari Mei sampai September 2026, dengan tingkat kematian kasus yang bertahan di sekitar 48 persen sejak Agustus. Organisasi MSF (Dokter Lintas Batas) mencatat angka yang sedikit berbeda per 1 September 2026 6.250 kasus dan 3.039 kematian bukan karena datanya bertentangan, tapi karena tanggal pengambilan datanya berbeda dari laporan WHO. Belum ada proyeksi resmi dari WHO soal kapan wabah ini akan terkendali.

Soal dana bantuan AS yang dipotong, angkanya juga berbeda-beda tergantung sumbernya. Refugees International mencatat penurunan dari 906 juta dolar AS (2024) ke sekitar 232 juta dolar AS (2026), sementara STAT News, mengutip data resmi USAID, mencatat pola berbeda: dari sekitar 1,2 miliar dolar AS (tahun fiskal 2024) turun menjadi hanya 67 juta dolar AS di tiga bulan terakhir 2025. Keduanya sepakat arahnya turun tajam tapi memakai metode hitung dan periode yang berbeda, jadi jangan menyamakan kedua angka itu begitu saja.

Yang juga belum diketahui: apakah kandidat vaksin dan antibodi monoklonal yang sedang diuji WHO sudah menunjukkan hasil, dan apakah ada personel TNI yang sempat terpapar selama penugasan di Mongbwalu. Riset ini juga tidak menemukan pernyataan resmi terpisah dari Kementerian Kesehatan atau Kementerian Luar Negeri Indonesia soal wabah ini, di luar konteks penugasan TNI.

Yang bisa kamu amati sendiri: pantau pembaruan resmi dari WHO atau ECDC secara berkala, bukan angka yang beredar di media sosial tanpa sumber jelas. Angka kasus dan kematian berubah nyaris setiap hari, apa yang benar hari ini bisa sudah berubah minggu depan.
Wabah ini belum ada tanggal akhirnya. Yang ada baru angka yang terus diperbarui — dan pasukan Indonesia yang masih di sana.

title: Jane Doe: Seeing Within the Cornell Case
excerpt: An unfinished case sits upon the honorable reputation of an Ivy League university. Cornell University said they had shared all investigative information, yet a police interview is said to have never been received by the district attorney. Now, New York’s governor has entrusted the case to the state’s attorney general.
coverImageAlt: Uris Library, McGraw Tower and Olin Library on the Cornell University campus in Ithaca, New York
coverImageCredit: Photo: P. Hughes / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 4.0)
author: UGS Newsroom

content.html: In a six-page statement to Cornell campus police, Jane Doe claimed that she was heavily intoxicated, was hit, and felt pressured into having sexual intercourse. She said she did not feel comfortable with part of an early encounter, but she did not consent to what came later, according to a copy CNN obtained from a source. She called the pressure coercion.

A group chat on Snapchat, an app where messages can disappear quickly, was active while the alleged assault was happening, according to images CNN obtained. The chat was titled "Chi Phi Actives," and one message in it includes a photo of Doe in a room at the house followed by inappropriate comments about what they ‘plan’ to do to her. A source close to the case said to CNN that other photos or videos might have been recovered in a more thorough criminal investigation.

Doe says she reported the alleged assault to Cornell police on Nov 8, 2024, according to a civil lawsuit filed in September 2026. Attorneys for two defendants named in that lawsuit told CBS New York their clients deny the charges.
"I've lost faith in the Tompkins County DA's ability to fairly oversee it." — Gov. Kathy Hochul, Oct 1, 2026

The case goes back to Oct 19, 2024, when, according to reporting by The New York Times cited by CNN, an alleged gang rape began in a room at the Chi Phi fraternity house at Cornell University in Ithaca, New York. The woman, referred to in news reports as Jane Doe, was then a student. She accused seven men. Attorneys for two defendants named in a civil lawsuit told CBS New York their clients deny the charges.

Doe reported the alleged assault to Cornell police on November 8, 2024, according to a civil complaint filed in September 2026. Police interviewed her on November 14 and 15, according to a transcript CBS New York obtained from a source. She signed a six-page statement. The district attorney of Tompkins County, Matthew Van Houten, later decided not to press charges. He says that decision rested on the statement.

content.html: Two processes followed her report, but they both ended in different ways. Cornell ran its own internal investigation, which led to expulsions, suspensions and other sanctions, according to CBS New York. Criminal prosecutors, however, did not bring charges. Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten says that decision rested on Doe's six-page statement, which he says multiple prosecutors and criminal investigators reviewed.

In late September 2026, CBS New York obtained a transcript of Jane Doe's interview with the campus police, which was held on November 14 and 15, 2024, from a source. According to the transcript, Doe said she had been drinking and using drugs, such as ketamine, but she had gaps in her memory, and did not remember the end of the night. She also said she did not know how many people had intercourse with her.
"I can say with 100% confidence I was raped." - Jane Doe, in a November 2024 campus police interview, according to a transcript obtained by CBS New York.

The two accounts of what the DA received do not match. Van Houten told CNN his office received no more than screenshots of Snapchat messages and the six-page report. Cornell says its police had followed protocol and shared all investigatory information with the DA. Though, the sources UGS reviewed do not establish who is right.

content.text: One transcript, but somehow, two different accounts of what reached the DA.

content.html: Former prosecutor Gary Galperin said the university likely had not broken any laws if it did not share every document, but the act of holding documents back would still fall short of basic standards of logic and decency, especially in a case involving multiple accusations. Former Westchester County District Attorney Mimi Rocah stated that an investigator trying to get at the truth should have sought more information.

Doe's attorney, Thomas Giuffra, says that the DA had enough evidence to act: a woman who told an officer she was raped, and a group chat that invited sexual assaults. The group chat ran on Snapchat, an app where messages disappear quickly. A source close to the case told CNN that a more thorough criminal investigation might have recovered other photos or videos. If you use similar apps, this case shows that a message sent in the moment can still be read later.

This case has two main components. One was Cornell's own formal disciplinary process, called a Title IX investigation, which is generally confidential and limited to the people involved. It led to expulsions, suspensions and other sanctions of the people involved. The other one was the criminal track,  where it was run though police and the district attorney, which ended in a decision not to bring any charges before prosecutors reopened it, according to CBS.

Cornell's Title IX file is large. According to The New York Times, as reported by CNN, it holds hundreds of pages of evidence in emails, text messages, photos and also interviews, including interviews with six of the seven men Doe accused of being the perpetrators. Doe's attorney says he does not know whether any of it has reached the police, and he says his office did not leak the documents to the Times. CNN also has not seen the Title IX filings.

The outcome of that process is itself contested. Doe's attorney says Cornell has expelled two of the seven accused students and given the others lesser punishments, allegedly in the form of essays. Cornell disputes part of that, saying none of the students charged by the university were offered an essay as their sole consequence. On the other hand, the Chi Phi national fraternity says its chapter voted unanimously to remove the accused members three days after Doe filed her police report, and Cornell says the chapter had been closed in 2024.

This is what you should keep an eye on. Van Houten says he will seek the transcript and follow up with Cornell police, and CBS reports that prosecutors have reopened the criminal investigation. Attorney General James now has the power and right to investigate and prosecute if warranted. Cornell has also agreed to an outside review of its handling of the case, according to Hochul, and the university confirmed it agreed but gave no further details.

Cornell focuses on one point in change. It says it set up a Presidential Task Force on Campus Sexual Assault in early 2025, made up of faculty, staff and students. Hayden Watkins, executive vice president of the Cornell Student Assembly, says the task force had roughly 20 members, only two of them undergraduates, and that students had very little voice.

The sources listed do not say what was handed to the district attorney, and CNN reports it is unclear whether any of the accused are still Cornell students. Everything about the night itself remains an allegation as a testimony from Doe.
This case is not merely about the events that happened that night, but it is also about the events that followed after. That is where the questions lie now.

id.title: Jane Doe: Melihat Lebih Dalam Kasus Cornell
id.excerpt: Sebuah kasus yang belum usai membayangi reputasi terhormat salah satu universitas Ivy League. Cornell University menyatakan telah menyerahkan seluruh informasi penyelidikan, namun pihak kejaksaan mengaku tak pernah menerima transkrip wawancara kepolisian. Kini, Gubernur New York telah menyerahkan penanganan kasus ini kepada Jaksa Agung negara bagian.

content.html: Dalam pernyataan enam halaman kepada polisi kampus Cornell, Jane Doe mengaku berada dalam keadaan sangat mabuk, dipukul, dan dipaksa melakukan hubungan seksual. Ia menyatakan tidak merasa nyaman sejak awal interaksi, tetapi tidak pernah memberikan persetujuan atas apa yang terjadi setelahnya, menurut salinan dokumen yang diperoleh CNN dari seorang sumber. Ia menyebut tekanan tersebut sebagai bentuk pemaksaan.

Grup obrolan di Snapchat, yaitu aplikasi tempat pesan dapat terhapus dengan cepat, tercatat aktif saat dugaan kekerasan seksual berlangsung, menurut tangkapan layar yang diperoleh CNN. Grup tersebut diberi nama "Chi Phi Actives," dan salah satu pesan memuat foto Doe di dalam sebuah kamar di rumah persaudaraan tersebut, diikuti komentar tidak pantas mengenai apa yang 'direncanakan' akan mereka lakukan terhadapnya. Seorang sumber yang dekat dengan kasus ini menyampaikan kepada CNN bahwa foto atau video lain mungkin bisa ditemukan jika dilakukan penyelidikan pidana yang lebih mendalam.

Doe menyatakan telah melaporkan dugaan kekerasan seksual ini kepada polisi Cornell pada 8 November 2024, menurut gugatan perdata yang diajukan pada September 2026. Pengacara dari dua tergugat yang dinamai dalam gugatan tersebut menyampaikan kepada CBS New York bahwa klien mereka membantah seluruh tuduhan.
"Saya telah kehilangan kepercayaan pada kemampuan Jaksa Wilayah Tompkins County untuk mengawasinya secara adil." — Gov. Kathy Hochul, Oct 1, 2026

Kasus ini bermula pada 19 Oktober 2024, ketika, menurut laporan The New York Times yang dikutip CNN, dugaan pemerkosaan bergilir dimulai di sebuah kamar di rumah persaudaraan Chi Phi di Cornell University, Ithaca, New York. Perempuan tersebut, yang dalam laporan berita disamarkan sebagai Jane Doe, saat itu merupakan seorang mahasiswa. Ia menuduh tujuh pria. Pengacara dari dua tergugat yang dinamai dalam gugatan perdata menyampaikan kepada CBS New York bahwa klien mereka membantah tuduhan tersebut.

Doe melaporkan dugaan kekerasan seksual tersebut kepada polisi Cornell pada 8 November 2024, menurut dokumen gugatan perdata yang diajukan pada September 2026. Polisi memewawancarainya pada 14 dan 15 November, menurut transkrip yang diperoleh CBS New York dari seorang sumber. Ia menandatangani pernyataan sepanjang enam halaman. Jaksa Wilayah Tompkins County, Matthew Van Houten, kemudian memutuskan untuk tidak mengajukan tuntutan pidana. Ia menyatakan keputusan itu didasarkan pada pernyataan tersebut.

content.html: Dua proses hukum dan administratif bergulir setelah laporannya, namun keduanya berakhir dengan hasil yang berbeda. Cornell menjalankan penyelidikan internal sendiri yang berujung pada sanksi pemecatan, skorsing, dan hukuman lainnya, menurut CBS New York. Namun, jaksa penuntut pidana tidak mengajukan dakwaan. Jaksa Wilayah Tompkins County, Matthew Van Houten, menyatakan keputusan itu didasarkan pada pernyataan enam halaman milik Doe, yang menurutnya telah ditinjau oleh beberapa jaksa dan penyidik pidana.

Pada akhir September 2026, CBS New York memperoleh transkrip wawancara Jane Doe dengan polisi kampus yang berlangsung pada 14 dan 15 November 2024 dari seorang sumber. Berdasarkan transkrip tersebut, Doe mengaku telah mengonsumsi alkohol dan obat-obatan, seperti ketamin, sehingga memiliki ingatan yang terputus-putus dan tidak mengingat kejadian di akhir malam. Ia juga menyatakan tidak mengetahui berapa banyak orang yang melakukan hubungan seksual dengannya.
"Saya bisa mengatakan dengan keyakinan 100% bahwa saya diperkosa." - Jane Doe, dalam wawancara dengan polisi kampus pada November 2024, menurut transkrip yang diperoleh CBS New York.

Dua keterangan mengenai apa yang diterima oleh Jaksa Wilayah saling bertolak belakang. Van Houten menyampaikan kepada CNN bahwa kantornya hanya menerima tangkapan layar pesan Snapchat dan laporan enam halaman. Cornell menyatakan pihak kepolisiannya telah mengikuti protokol dan membagikan seluruh informasi penyelidikan kepada Jaksa Wilayah. Meskipun demikian, sumber-sumber yang ditinjau UGS tidak dapat memastikan pihak mana yang benar.

content.text: Satu transkrip, tetapi ada dua versi berbeda mengenai dokumen yang sampai ke tangan Jaksa Wilayah.

content.html: Mantan jaksa penuntut Gary Galperin menyatakan bahwa pihak universitas kemungkinan tidak melanggar hukum jika tidak membagikan setiap dokumen, tetapi tindakan menahan dokumen tetap tidak memenuhi standar dasar logika dan kepatutan, terutama dalam kasus yang melibatkan banyak tuduhan. Mantan Jaksa Wilayah Westchester County, Mimi Rocah, menegaskan bahwa seorang penyidik yang berusaha mencari kebenaran seharusnya mencari informasi lebih lanjut.

Pengacara Doe, Thomas Giuffra, menyatakan bahwa Jaksa Wilayah memiliki cukup bukti untuk bertindak: seorang perempuan yang memberi tahu petugas bahwa ia diperkosa, dan sebuah grup obrolan yang mengarah pada tindakan kekerasan seksual. Grup obrolan tersebut berjalan di Snapchat, aplikasi tempat pesan terhapus dengan cepat. Seorang sumber yang dekat dengan kasus ini menyampaikan kepada CNN bahwa penyelidikan pidana yang lebih mendalam mungkin bisa menemukan foto atau video lainnya. Jika kamu menggunakan aplikasi serupa, kasus ini menunjukkan bahwa pesan yang dikirim dalam suatu momen masih bisa dibaca di kemudian hari.

Kasus ini memiliki dua komponen utama. Pertama adalah proses disiplin formal internal Cornell yang disebut penyelidikan Title IX, yang umumnya bersifat rahasia dan terbatas pada pihak-pihak yang terlibat. Proses ini berujung pada pemecatan, skorsing, dan sanksi lain bagi orang-orang yang terlibat. Komponen lainnya adalah jalur pidana yang dijalankan melalui kepolisian dan jaksa wilayah, yang berakhir dengan keputusan untuk tidak mengajukan tuntutan sebelum akhirnya dibuka kembali oleh jaksa penuntut, menurut CBS.

Berkas Title IX milik Cornell sangat tebal. Menurut The New York Times sebagaimana dilaporkan CNN, berkas itu berisi ratusan halaman bukti berupa email, pesan teks, foto, serta wawancara, termasuk wawancara dengan enam dari tujuh pria yang dituduh Doe sebagai pelaku. Pengacara Doe menyatakan tidak mengetahui apakah ada dokumen tersebut yang telah sampai ke tangan polisi, dan ia menegaskan kantornya tidak membocorkan dokumen itu kepada The New York Times. CNN juga belum melihat berkas permohonan Title IX tersebut.

Hasil dari proses tersebut sendiri masih diperdebatkan. Pengacara Doe menyatakan Cornell telah mengeluarkan dua dari tujuh mahasiswa yang dituduh dan memberikan hukuman yang lebih ringan kepada mahasiswa lainnya, yang diduga berupa penulisan esai. Cornell membantah sebagian hal itu, dengan menyatakan bahwa tidak ada mahasiswa yang dijatuhi sanksi oleh universitas yang hanya diberi hukuman menulis esai sebagai satu-satunya konsekuensi. Di sisi lain, organisasi persaudaraan nasional Chi Phi menyatakan bahwa anggotanya memilih secara bulat untuk mengeluarkan para anggota yang tertuduh tiga hari setelah Doe membuat laporan polisi, dan Cornell menyatakan bahwa cabang tersebut telah ditutup pada tahun 2024.

Inilah hal-hal yang perlu kamu pantau. Van Houten menyatakan ia akan meminta transkrip tersebut dan menindaklanjutinya dengan polisi Cornell, dan CBS melaporkan bahwa jaksa penuntut telah membuka kembali penyelidikan pidana. Jaksa Agung James kini memiliki kewenangan dan hak untuk menyelidiki serta menuntut jika ditemukan bukti yang cukup. Cornell juga telah menyetujui peninjauan independen eksternal atas penanganan kasus ini, menurut Hochul, dan pihak universitas membenarkan persetujuan tersebut namun tidak memberikan rincian lebih lanjut.

Cornell berfokus pada satu langkah perubahan. Universitas menyatakan telah membentuk Satuan Tugas Presiden untuk Kekerasan Seksual di Kampus pada awal 2025, yang terdiri dari dosen, staf, dan mahasiswa. Hayden Watkins, wakil presiden eksekutif dari Cornell Student Assembly, menyatakan bahwa satuan tugas tersebut memiliki sekitar 20 anggota, dengan hanya dua di antaranya mahasiswa sarjana, sehingga mahasiswa memiliki suara yang sangat minim.

Sumber-sumber yang terdaftar tidak menyebutkan apa yang sebenarnya diserahkan kepada jaksa wilayah, dan CNN melaporkan belum jelas apakah ada dari para tertuduh yang masih berstatus sebagai mahasiswa Cornell. Seluruh rincian mengenai peristiwa malam itu tetap berstatus sebagai tuduhan berdasarkan kesaksian dari Doe.
Kasus ini bukan sekadar mengenai peristiwa yang terjadi pada malam itu, melainkan juga tentang apa yang terjadi setelahnya. Di situlah muara pertanyaan besar saat ini.

title: Bali’s Pertalite Queues: The Cause Is Still Disputed
excerpt: You may not live in Bali. But Pertalite, Indonesia’s subsidized gasoline, costs the same Rp10,000 per liter there as it does across the country. When its delivery stalls, some pumps can run dry.
coverImageAlt: A Pertamina gas station in Bali
author: UGS Newsroom

content.html: You may not live in Bali. But Pertalite, Indonesia’s subsidized gasoline, costs the same Rp10,000 per liter there as it does across the country. When its delivery stalls, some pumps can run dry.

Since early October 2026, a number of public fuel filling stations (SPBU) in Bali have run out of Pertalite, the subsidized gasoline many motorbike riders use. On October 8, 2026, Pertamina Patra Niaga (Pertamina’s distribution unit) acknowledged that Pertalite supply had earlier been delayed. Queues peaked on October 12 and 13, 2026, mainly in Denpasar and Badung. Reports on how long they were differ: about one kilometer according to Yahoo News Australia and detik, three kilometers according to iNews.

On October 13, 2026, Pertamina President Director Simon Aloysius Mantiri apologized to Bali residents in Denpasar. He named a problem unloading ships, caused by an anchor issue, as one of the causes. That same day, 92 SPBU in Denpasar and Badung were asked to open 24 hours. According to Media Indonesia, Pertamina increased its tanker trucks from 90 to 105 units. Bali Governor I Wayan Koster, who summoned Pertamina to his official residence on October 12, 2026, said stocks were sufficient and asked residents not to panic.

Pertamina scheduled three ships for October 12, 14 and 16, 2026, adding a total of 26,200 kiloliters. One kiloliter equals 1,000 liters. Sources disagree on which ship arrived when. Jakarta Globe wrote that two ships carrying a combined 21.7 million liters had arrived, and that one of them, the MT Klasogun, docked on October 13, 2026. Pertamina, via detikBali, said a ship carrying 18,000 kiloliters of Pertalite and 2,500 kiloliters of unsubsidized Pertamax had already arrived on October 11. The Downstream Oil and Gas Regulatory Agency (BPH Migas) said unloading of the Pertalite ship was completed on October 13, 2026.

content.html: Those hit hardest are people who depend on vehicles in Bali. Queues of several hours disrupt drivers and businesses. According to Barometer Bali on October 14, 2026, some residents stayed in line since the day before, and a few SPBU ran out of fuel. The economic impact has no figures from official sources yet, so UGS does not estimate it. Pertamina explained that recovery takes time because fuel must be shipped by tanker before it is sent on to stations.
Fuel in a terminal and fuel in the pump are different things. The queues happened in the gap between them.

The link to you is price. Pertalite sells for Rp10,000 per liter across Indonesia, unchanged as of October 10, 2026. Pertamax, an unsubsidized gasoline priced at market rates, sells for Rp15,950 per liter in Java since September 2, 2026, according to iNews. The gap is Rp5,950 per liter.

A gap that size has effects. After Pertamax rose to Rp16,250 on June 10, 2026, one expert called its distance from Pertalite, Rp6,250, the widest in history. Several sources link that price gap to riders switching to Pertalite. In Medan in July 2026, Pertamina said the gap between subsidized and unsubsidized prices also raised demand. For Bali, no source yet shows a direct link to these queues.

In Surakarta, UGS found no reports of fuel disruption in October 2026. On April 2, 2026, RRI Surakarta reported that Solo (Surakarta’s common name) residents were not panic buying, meaning buying more than needed out of fear of running out, when rumors of a fuel price rise circulated. So for now the link to your city runs through prices and national policy, not queues outside your home.

content.text: Officials say there is enough fuel. Some pumps are empty.

content.html: The cause of these queues is disputed, and there are three versions. Bali Governor I Wayan Koster pointed to a surge in demand, panic buying and delivery trucks stuck in traffic. Pertamina pointed to trouble unloading ships. Fathul Nugroho, a member of the BPH Migas committee, said the queues were triggered by operational problems when unloading a Pertalite ship, not a shortage of stock, and that unloading was finished on October 13, 2026. Rilke Jeffri Huwae, a Director General at the Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources (ESDM), also said the problem lay in distribution and ship operations, not in falling national stock. Laode Sulaeman, Director General of Oil and Gas, said in general terms that high waves can hinder ships from docking, without tying it directly to Bali.

This kind of disruption is not new. In late August 2026, Pertalite queues also formed in Denpasar and Badung. Pertamina then linked them to adjusted ship docking schedules at two fuel terminals, the storage sites from which fuel is sent to stations, Manggis and Sanggaran. In November 2025, Bali ran short of fuel because bad weather forced ships to take a longer route. On October 8, 2026, Pertamina said it was adjusting supply patterns and routes without saying what had changed.

The wider context lies outside Bali. In March 2026, war in the Middle East led to the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, a narrow sea route through which much of the world’s oil passes, according to Tempo and Al Jazeera. On October 9, 2026, Director General of Oil and Gas Laode Sulaeman said Indonesia had lost about 25 percent of its fuel import sources since that war, so the government is now seeking fuel directly from countries with surplus stock. National stock is put at 18 to 20 days according to Laode, and 18 to 21 days according to Energy and Mineral Resources Minister Bahlil Lahadalia. No source yet ties any of this directly to Bali.

Those most exposed are riders in Denpasar and Badung, where 92 SPBU were asked to operate 24 hours. Pertamina plans to extend 24-hour service to Tabanan and Gianyar within one to two days. Pertamina also asked stations to post notices about stock and operating hours. According to Media Indonesia, Pertamina is also coordinating with police to escort fuel deliveries.

The next thing to watch is the third ship, scheduled for October 16, 2026. On October 14, 2026, Koster said Pertalite and Pertamax stocks in Bali were safe for up to two weeks. A UGS calculation gives a different picture: if Jakarta Globe’s figure of 19.2 million liters of Pertalite is right and daily consumption is 2.2 million liters according to Pertamina, that load equals about 8.7 days of Pertalite. This is a UGS estimate, not official data, and the ship figure itself is disputed. Pertamina also said station operating patterns could be reviewed if the situation stabilizes within two to three days, according to Media Indonesia.

Some things are still unknown. On October 14, 2026, BPH Migas said Bali was returning to normal and terminal stocks had recovered, while Barometer Bali reported that queues were still long and fuel trucks were late. The cause of the anchor problem has not been explained either. When the queues will truly end has not been confirmed.
The queue at the pump is the part you can see. The rest happens at sea and on the road, between the ship, the terminal and the station.
